A.explanation: This is lower than $250 \text{ Hz}$ and would suit a receding source with denominator $v + v_s$, not an approaching train.

B.explanation: This is also lower than the source frequency, whereas an approaching source compresses the waves and raises the observed frequency above $250 \text{ Hz}$.

C.explanation: This is close to $250 \times (340+80)/340$, which is the formula for a moving observer, not for the moving source here.

D.explanation: An approaching source gives $f_o = f_s v/(v - v_s) = 250 \times 340/260 \approx 327 \text{ Hz}$, closest to $330 \text{ Hz}$.

hints: Notice the source at $80 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is moving toward the stationary observer, so successive wavefronts are crowded together and observed wavelength is shorter.
Connect this to the moving-source Doppler rule where the effective wavelength is $v/f_s - v_s/f_s$, giving $f_o = f_s v/(v - v_s)$ for approaching.
Next calculate the denominator $340 - 80 = 260 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, then evaluate $250 \times 340/260$ and round to the nearest option.
walkthrough: Identify the givens: source frequency $f_s = 250 \text{ Hz}$, speed of sound $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, source speed $v_s = 80 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ toward a stationary observer.

State the rule: for a source approaching a stationary observer the observed wavelength is shortened to $\lambda_o = (v - v_s)/f_s$, so observed frequency $f_o = v/\lambda_o = f_s v/(v - v_s)$ is greater than $f_s$.
Set up the calculation with a minus sign because approaching reduces the denominator: $f_o = 250 \times 340/(340 - 80)$.
Substitute values with units: denominator $= 340 - 80 = 260 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $f_o = 250 \times 340/260$.
Show the intermediate result: $340/260 \approx 1.308$, so $f_o \approx 250 \times 1.308 \approx 327 \text{ Hz}$ with unit $\text{Hz}$ as required.
Compare to the options $190 \text{ Hz}$, $200 \text{ Hz}$, $310 \text{ Hz}$, $330 \text{ Hz}$: $327 \text{ Hz}$ is closest to $330 \text{ Hz}$. This is option D.
